pull_request.title: ci: install dylint tools as prebuilt binaries via taiki-e/install-action
pull_request.body:
## Description

Every run of the Lint workflow compiled `cargo-dylint` and `dylint-link` from source via `cargo install`, adding several minutes of pure waste to each push and PR. This PR replaces that with prebuilt binary installation to cut CI time substantially and speed up the contributor feedback loop.

## Changes

- **`.github/workflows/lint.yml`**: Replaced `run: cargo install cargo-dylint dylint-link` with `uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2` and `tool: cargo-dylint,dylint-link`.
- The existing `Swatinem/rust-cache@v2` step was **already present** in the workflow, so no changes were needed there.

## Why `taiki-e/install-action`

- Downloads prebuilt binaries from GitHub Releases → completes in **seconds** instead of minutes
- Automatically **falls back to `cargo install`** if no prebuilt binary exists for the target platform
- Widely adopted in the Rust ecosystem (tokio-rs, crossbeam, etc.)
- Clean, single-line syntax for installing multiple tools

## Behavior

- ✅ **Cache hit**: Prebuilt binaries install in seconds; cached cargo target/registry speeds up `cargo test --workspace` and `cargo clippy`
- ✅ **Cache miss / first run**: `taiki-e/install-action` falls back to `cargo install`; rust-cache populates on first run — workflow remains correct
- ✅ **No functional changes**: The workflow still runs: `checkout` → `rust-toolchain` → `rust-cache` → `fmt` → `clippy` → `install dylint` → `test`

Closes #13
